subject: Re: Kickoff: node-level DP GNNs for interaction-graph features
body:
Status.

Reproduction: done, about three weeks in. DP-GCN on ogbn-arxiv from configs/dpgcn.py matches the reported accuracy band, and the config_flags overrides made the epsilon sweep painless -- we ran 6 privacy budgets by just overriding num_training_steps and the noise parameters per run.

The substantive finding: the utility cliff is sharper on our anonymized interaction subgraph than on ogbn-arxiv. At the epsilon Legal is likely to ask for, we lose 9 points of task accuracy vs. the non-private baseline, compared to a 4-point loss on ogbn-arxiv at the same budget. High-degree nodes are exactly the informative ones, and node-level DP clips their influence hardest.

Risk: if Legal anchors on the strictest epsilon, the feature teams may conclude the features are not worth shipping. The epsilon-vs-utility curve needs to go to both parties together, not Legal first.

Maren
